provenance.paper_title: PyraVid: Hierarchical Multimodal Memory for Long-Horizon Video Reasoning

representation_paths.memory_component: fact nodes with associated visual evidence

evidence.paraphrase: Each fact node stores temporal information, associated visual evidence, grounded text, and links to related nodes.

representation_paths.memory_component: fact, clip, and global textual-structured memory

evidence.paraphrase: Fact, clip, and evolving global levels are linked across granularity and by logical relations; inference expands and prunes evidence until sufficient.

Clip nodes summarize local events and the global node incrementally integrates clip-level context. For PyraVid, this specifically supports episodic or hierarchical summarization of fact nodes with associated visual evidence.

New facts are connected to clip/global parents and sparsely linked to logically related facts. For PyraVid, this specifically supports relinking or reindexing of stored items of fact nodes with associated visual evidence.

Character-level memory is incrementally rewritten and profiled as new face and voice evidence arrives. For PyraVid, this specifically supports LLM-mediated memory editing of fact nodes with associated visual evidence.

derived.hybrid_relation: Coarse textual abstractions and graph links retain a route to the visual evidence stored in fact nodes.

adjudication_notes: Strict-tier full-paper review (PDF p. 4): During inference, the operative memory component (fact nodes with associated visual evidence) changes through episodic or hierarchical summarization, relinking or reindexing of stored items, LLM-mediated memory editing; the governing policy remains fixed, and any learning reported by the paper occurs before deployment. Training-time learning, when present, was not counted as T3.
